metadata.title: [Perf][SM75][Build] Pin the Turing FlashAttention library to the split-wave heuristic
metadata.body:
## Purpose

The Turing FlashAttention library picks its split-KV count with num_splits_heuristic, which multiplies the SM count by a hard-coded 2 CTAs per SM. For head dim 256 on Turing the 64 x 32 kernel uses exactly 64 KB of shared memory, so one CTA fits per SM: the heuristic planned 144 slots on 72 SMs, and with two KV heads and a 236,000-token context it chose 62 splits = 124 CTAs, a second wave of 52 CTAs after a full one.

The commit this PR pins derives the resident CTAs per SM from the kernel's shared memory tiles, capped at 2 as before, and chooses the split count with the fewest KV blocks streamed in sequence. For that shape it gives 36 splits = 72 CTAs, one full wave.

This PR changes one line: VLLM_FLASH_ATTN_SM75_COMMIT moves from 43b9d29c9 to 6ab41c291 (github.com/Peuqui/flash-attention, branch splitkv-wave-heuristic), the repository main already pins.

Not a duplicate: searched the open PRs of this repository (86 at the time of writing) for num_splits_heuristic, split-KV and flash_attn_sm75. #1279 and #1286 appear for their own split-KV paths in another kernel and do not change this pin.

AI assistance was used for this change. I reviewed the change and ran the measurements below.

## Test Plan

The library built on its own from github.com/Peuqui/flash-attention at the new commit is the one our fork has run in production since 2026-10-31; the kernel measurement and the model series below used it. I did not build this PR's CMake path here: the pin only moves to another commit of the same repository, reachable on its branch splitkv-wave-heuristic (git ls-remote).
pre-commit run --from-ref origin/main --to-ref HEAD
pre-commit run mypy-3.10 --all-files --hook-stage manual

## Path coverage

| Path / provider | Format | Key conditions (shape, TP/EP, graph, capability) | Expected selection / fallback | Evidence (source / static / executed / measured) | Unverified scope |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| FLASH_ATTN decode on SM75 through the Turing library | fp16 KV, head dim 256 | split-KV, long context, several KV heads | 36 instead of 62 splits at the measured shape | measured: kernel in CUDA graphs and model series | other Turing SM counts than 72 |
| same | other head dims | shared memory allows 2 CTAs per SM | same assumption as before, new choice rule | source | not measured |

## Acceleration and benchmark contract (required for performance changes)

- Default enabled or opt-in: default enabled, no switch, through the pin.
- Required CLI options and environment switches: none. Benchmark entry: Qwen3.8-27B NVFP4, --tensor-parallel-size 2 on two Quadro RTX 8000, MTP with 3 speculative tokens, attention_backend FLASH_ATTN.
- KV cache dtype used for the benchmark: the entry's default, fp16.
- Wheel SHA or source commit: library commit 6ab41c291 in the changed arm. vLLM fork build: reference tag verified-2026-10-28-prod-v5, changed ea2ec07f6, one commit later, a fix for nested outputs of DFlash-type drafters that this MTP entry does not reach.
- PYTHONPATH, source overlays, or external native libraries used: the fork tree and a patched Triton 3.6 build on PYTHONPATH in both arms; between the arms the Turing FlashAttention library and that one commit differ.
- User-entry route-hit, speed, and output-quality evidence: OpenAI API server entry, below.
- Existing kernel/backend registry and capability-rejection reasons: not touched.
- Per-engine configuration and deprecated-variable compatibility: no new or changed setting.
- New/changed environment metadata and generated reference check: none.
- Route snapshot command and intentional changed rows: none.
- SM70 registered variables / unregistered reads / model-parameter restrictions, before -> after: no change.

## Test Result

Kernel on a Quadro RTX 8000 in CUDA graphs (2 KV heads, 6 query heads per KV head, 24 packed rows, 832-token pages), ms per call, lower is better, the 62 splits of the former rule against 36: 236,000 tokens 1.494 -> 1.292, 100,000 tokens 0.669 -> 0.571, 33,000 tokens 0.257 -> 0.217. 37 splits, a second wave of two CTAs, took 2.18 ms. Outputs equal up to 1.5e-5.

Qwen3.8-27B on two RTX 8000 (TP2, MTP), runs T T P T P through the same server entry, counted T#2 + T#4 against P#3 + P#5, ms per decode round (lower is better):
- 33,208 tokens: 34.5 / 34.4 changed, 35.3 / 35.2 reference.
- 184,134 tokens: 49.4 / 49.4 changed, 52.5 / 52.5 reference.
- 249,992 tokens: 57.0 / 57.1 changed, 60.4 / 60.4 reference.
- 259,552 tokens: 58.1 / 57.9 changed, 62.1 / 61.3 reference.

Prefill of 8,490 tokens 5.52 / 5.52 s (1,538 / 1,539 tok/s) changed, 5.53 / 5.53 s (1,535 / 1,535 tok/s) reference. Memory peak 48,331 MiB per card in all arms, KV pool 1,040,933 tokens. GSM8K-30 29/30 changed, 28/30 reference.

pre-commit run --from-ref origin/main --to-ref HEAD on this branch (main 4d57473db plus this commit; it merges cleanly into main 6db9c816c): every hook passes except check-layering, which reports vllm/model_executor/layers/fused_moe/runner/moe_runner.py (platform coupling 37 -> 39) exactly as main 4d57473db does. pre-commit run mypy-3.10 --all-files --hook-stage manual: no issues.

🤖 Generated with Claude Code (https://claude.com/claude-code)

https://claude.ai/code/session_0172gtUkBtN8FSrthHLCZe8W
